title: Global Workforce Skill Gap Analysis for EdTech Expansion
business: A global vocational training platform planning to expand its curriculum into emerging markets.
problem: The company lacks granular data on which specific professional tasks are currently being prioritized by Claude users in target regions, leading to a mismatch between course offerings and actual labor market demand.
solution: By integrating the Anthropic Economic Index connector, the platform can programmatically query regional usage patterns and task breakdowns to identify high-growth professional domains, ensuring curriculum development aligns with real-world Claude interaction trends.
steps: Authenticate the Anthropic Economic Index connector within the Claude environment to gain read-only access to the public dataset.
Execute econ_index_list_countries to filter for target emerging markets.
Call econ_index_get_occupation_usage and econ_index_list_top_work_tasks for each identified country to extract task-specific usage patterns.
Aggregate the retrieved task data to map current user interest against existing course modules.
Compare regional findings using econ_index_compare_regions to prioritize market entry based on shared skill demand.
outcome: The platform achieves a data-driven strategy for curriculum localization, reducing the risk of launching training programs that do not address the specific professional needs of the target workforce.
limitation: The dataset is strictly read-only and reflects historical usage patterns, meaning it cannot predict future market shifts or provide real-time user intent; verify findings by cross-referencing with local labor bureau reports.
